zh: 先严格筛掉格式错误的行，它们的路径对既不参与连通，也不参与歧义判断。合法行要同时满足：按单个空格切出的词数为偶数且至少 4 个；第 1、3 个词是 id 和 timestamp；第 2、4 个词全是数字；所有键（id、timestamp 和每对里的路径）互不相同。
仓库就是“共享同一个 (路径, 标识) 对”关系下的连通块：用哈希表记下每个对第一次出现的提交，之后再出现就用并查集与它合并。歧义检查必须等所有合并结束后再做，因为两个提交可能稍后才被第三个提交连到一起。
合并完后，以 (根, 路径) 为键记录标识，同一键遇到不同标识就只输出 AMBIGUOUS INPUT!。否则把每个连通块的提交按 (时间戳, 编号) 排序；查询时用哈希表找到 (path, opaqueId) 所在的块，二分出第一个时间戳 ≥ start 的位置，向后输出直到时间戳 > end，每个编号后跟一个空格，没有结果也要输出空行。
en: First strictly filter out malformed lines; their path pairs take part in neither connectivity nor the ambiguity check. A valid line must satisfy all of: an even number of words, at least 4, when split on single spaces; the 1st and 3rd words are id and timestamp; the 2nd and 4th words are all digits; all keys (id, timestamp and the path of every pair) are pairwise distinct.

A repository is a connected component under the relation "shares an identical (path, identifier) pair": use a hash map to remember the first commit in which each pair appears, and union any later occurrence with it using union-find. The ambiguity check must wait until all merges are done, because two commits may only be connected later by a third commit.

After merging, record the identifier under the key (root, path); if one key meets two different identifiers, print only AMBIGUOUS INPUT!. Otherwise sort each component's commits by (timestamp, id). For a query, find the component of (path, opaqueId) through the hash map, binary search the first position with timestamp ≥ start, and print onward until the timestamp exceeds end, each id followed by a space; print an empty line when nothing qualifies.

explanationEn:
## Restating the problem

First filter out malformed log lines, then connect the remaining commits into connected components by "sharing the same (path, opaque identifier) pair"; each connected component is one repository. If some connected component has the same path with two different identifiers, the whole input is ambiguous and only AMBIGUOUS INPUT! is printed. Otherwise, for each query, find the repository containing that (path, identifier) and print the ids of the commits whose timestamps lie in the closed interval [start, end], in ascending order of (timestamp, id), each id followed by one space.

## Deciding whether a line is valid

Split on single spaces. A valid line has at least 4 words and an even word count; the 1st and 3rd words are id and timestamp respectively; the 2nd and 4th words are all digits; all keys (id, timestamp and the path in each pair) are pairwise distinct. If any condition fails, the whole line is discarded, and its path pairs take part in neither connectivity nor the ambiguity check.

## Algorithm

1. Number the valid commits one by one and maintain connected components with union-find. Use a hash map to record the first commit in which each (path, identifier) appears; when it appears again later, merge with that commit.
2. After all merges are done, scan every path pair of every commit again, recording the identifier under the key (root, path); meeting a different identifier means the input is ambiguous. The check must come after merging is complete, because two commits may first belong to different components and only later be connected by a third commit.
3. Sort the commits of each connected component by (timestamp, id). For a query, use the hash map to find the component of the anchor, binary search for the first position with timestamp ≥ start, and print onward until the timestamp is > end.

## Correctness

The edges merged by union-find are exactly the relation "shares the same path pair", so the final sets are exactly the connected components defined by the problem. Ambiguity depends only on the set of identifiers of each path within the final connected components, and step 2 checks every path pair of every component. After sorting, the commits whose timestamps lie in the interval form one contiguous run, and binary search plus a sequential scan prints exactly them, in the required order.

## Complexity

Let P be the total number of path pairs on valid lines and K the total number of ids printed by the queries. Merging and the ambiguity check take expected O(P·α), sorting O(N log N), and each query O(log N + number of results), for O((N+P)·α + N log N + R log N + K) in total.

## Independent verification

The oracle decides valid lines with a regular expression, finds connected components with BFS on the bipartite "commit to path pair" graph, then collects the identifier set of each path per component to detect ambiguity, and answers a query by filtering the whole component and sorting, using neither union-find nor binary search. Every combination of 1..3 valid commits with paths {f,g}, identifiers {1,2} and timestamps {1,2} is enumerated and the reference program is run on each; random data mixes in all kinds of malformed lines (wrong prefixes, non-digits, odd word counts, repeated keys, too short). Five wrong programs (accepting lines with an odd word count, not checking repeated keys, sorting by id only, ignoring ambiguity, an open interval at the end time) all exit normally and are judged wrong by the formal data.
